purpose: Start / bring up / launch the whole bundle stack from one command on a single host, no GPU (scope item 8). Renders env, makes certs, renders gateway config, starts core then all services, waits healthy, post-up reconcile.
Stop the bundle stack (docker compose down). State volumes are retained.
Follow the bundle's logs (docker compose logs -f --tail=100).
List the bundle's running services and their health (docker compose ps).
Run the scope-item test suite against the running bundle. These are the adjudication evidence for the nine outcomes.
Reconcile identity into virtual keys. Idempotent. (POST /admin/sync)
The one bill. Show spend across every provider. (GET /admin/spend)
The one audit trail, plus a chain verification. (GET /admin/audit/verify)
Export the ledger and verify it. Non-destructive — run it whenever.
Write the direct-provider configuration for each surface (so surfaces can run on direct provider keys instead of the gateway).
Leave the platform: export, verify, write direct config, then revoke every virtual key. DESTRUCTIVE — surfaces stop working until they hold direct provider keys.
Destroy all state including the databases. NOT reversible (docker compose down -v + removes realm export).
Reload Forge credentials from 1Password and regenerate the gateway model catalog.
Live smoke tests against Forge. Spends real money (fractions of a cent). Kept out of `make test`.
Full browser journey against the live k3s cluster: login, chat, agent writes a file, run gate, publish, fetch published link with no session. Needs workspaces provisioned.
Drive both UIs in a real Chromium against the live cluster; fails on any console error.
Sign in to CHAT (not the portal) from a fresh browser context against the real public origin, reload, and assert the session survives (cookie-policy defect).
Drive both browser-terminal workspaces as a person would, against the live cluster. Needs workspaces provisioned first.
A never-signed-in Keycloak account through the documented front door: a real assistant reply grounded in a real tool call, read back from the persisted message.
Thin wrapper for calling the control-plane admin API from the host. e.g. api.sh GET /admin/spend | api.sh POST /admin/sync '{...}'
Export the ledger and verify it (safe, non-destructive).
Write the direct-provider configuration for each surface.
Revoke every virtual key at the gateway. DESTRUCTIVE — requires --confirm.
The full exit: all three (export, direct, revoke) in the order that keeps surfaces working. DESTRUCTIVE — requires --confirm.
Create or update a realm user in the local bundle via the admin API. Idempotent.
Generate a self-signed TLS certificate for the identity provider. Required, not cosmetic: the chat OIDC client refuses plaintext discovery. Idempotent.
First-run reconcile, then print where everything is. Called automatically by `make up`.
Mint the chat surface's virtual key and write it into .env. Idempotent.
Mint rag-api's virtual key and write it into .env. Idempotent.
Ensure .env exists and every required secret has a value, then render config templates that need a secret. Fills gaps rather than regenerating. Called first by `make up`.
Render the gateway model catalog from Forge's live catalog and price list into litellm/config.generated.yaml. (Same as `make forge-config`.)
Generate/fill the codeapi Ed25519 keypairs that .env needs, in place.
Run the scope-item test suite against the running bundle (creates .venv-test on first use). Same as `make test`.
Verify an exported ledger. Standalone: stdlib only, talks to no running service.
Block until every service with a healthcheck reports healthy, or fail loudly.
Deploy the bundle to the k3s cluster. Reuses bundle/.env as the source of secrets so cluster and local compose can't drift. PUBLIC_BASE_URL must be the URL a browser will use (https, or login fails).
Post-deploy reconcile for the cluster — the k8s equivalent of post-up.sh (realm redirect URIs, bootstrap user, key sync via Keycloak admin API). Idempotent.
Prove the deployment can actually serve a prompt (exercises the real credential path with a live inference call). Run at the end of every deploy — 'pods Running' is not the same claim.
Register the portal's Keycloak client and put its secrets where the pod can read them. Idempotent; re-run after changing PUBLIC_BASE_URL.
Create a realm user on the cluster so multi-user isolation can be demonstrated. Password stored only in that user's own workspace-user-<username> Secret.
Create / make / set up / onboard one user's new browser-terminal (IDE) workspace on the cluster. Repeatable/idempotent; rotates a fresh <username>::ide virtual key each run.
Provision one named RESIDENT agent instance (INTEGRATED mode — gateway-metered per-agent virtual key).
Provision a resident agent in BYO mode: the user's own provider credential, no gateway ledger row.
ONE COMMAND: a resident agent, on the metered Forge path, talking in the company's chat (Slack or Discord). Composes provision-agent + the pod's chat tools.
Worked example: bring up a Slack-connected resident agent 'hermes' for user baron.
Build an image in the cluster with kaniko and push it to the rail registry (no Docker socket; context carried as a gzipped tar in a ConfigMap). For small contexts.
Continuous deployment: one pass; deploys the cluster if main went green, exits 0 if nothing to do. Intended to run on a timer on a host that can reach the cluster.
Force a cluster deploy even if this SHA was already deployed.
PRECONDITION: restore the 1Password session so Forge credentials load. Run this first on a cold shell, then `direnv reload`.
PRECONDITION: allow this repo's .envrc once so direnv loads the Forge env references.
PRECONDITION: reload the repo env after `op signin` so the FORGE_* vars populate in the shell.
Complete uninstall of the cluster deployment: delete the whole enterprise-ai namespace.
Reach the unpublished control-plane admin API from your machine (then call /admin/spend, /admin/sync, etc against localhost:8081).
DELETE / reclaim / tear down one user's existing workspace objects on the cluster (deploy, svc, pvc, secret for that user).
Stop a resident agent (scale to zero); its PVC is retained so it can resume.
Start / resume a resident agent (scale back to one replica).
Stage a gateway-VM Caddy edge-config change: copy the repo Caddyfile to the gateway host.
Validate, back up, install and reload the gateway VM's Caddy config over ssh (edge/ingress change).
command: ssh baron@gateway ' sudo caddy validate --adapter caddyfile --config /tmp/Caddyfile.new && sudo cp -a /etc/caddy/Caddyfile /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S) && sudo cp /tmp/Caddyfile.new /etc/caddy/Caddyfile && sudo systemctl reload caddy'
